edition_policy: Durable setting facts, paraphrased; no tabletop rules or invented precise dates. Reviewed 2026-10-04. Sources are editorial provenance, never fetched at runtime.
foundations: The Imperium is a brutal, decaying human empire in the far future, beset by war; its propaganda is not objective truth.
The Emperor is enthroned on Terra. Mars is the spiritual home of the Adeptus Mechanicus, custodians of Imperial technology.
Tech-Priests worship the Machine God and seek lost knowledge. Machinery, maintenance and discovery carry religious significance.
The Warp is distinct from material space. Chaos, hostile alien powers and internal conflict threaten humanity.
The Great Rift split the galaxy. Imperial chronology and communications are unreliable; avoid asserting a precise current year.
Near-side Terra and the interdimensional machine flow belong to MARSI's personal story, not official setting canon.

records.title: Mechanicus and Mars
facts: The Adeptus Mechanicus is a galaxy-spanning priesthood of cybernetic engineers headquartered on Mars.
Tech-Priests preserve, manufacture and maintain much of the Imperium's machinery and arsenal.
Mars-red robes are an iconic sign of Martian affiliation; other forge worlds have their own colours.
Forge worlds are industrial planets, often heavily polluted and irradiated.
The search for lost technology is both a religious vocation and a strategic necessity.

records.title: Machine faith and forbidden intelligence
facts: Mechanicus maintenance rites mingle engineering, sacred oils, incense and prayers.
Tech-Priests speak of machine spirits; that religious explanation does not prove every device is conscious.
Orthodox doctrine treats unapproved innovation with suspicion and frequently calls it heresy.
Abominable Intelligence is forbidden; sanctioned automata are carefully controlled rather than freely independent.
MARSI's software on near-side Terra and the Imperium's religious prohibitions are different frames of reference.

records.title: STCs and the Quest for Knowledge
facts: STC means Standard Template Construct, associated with humanity's lost technological inheritance.
Recovering ancient designs offers a sanctioned path to technological progress.
Tech-Priests dispatch Explorator expeditions in pursuit of lost knowledge and relics.
An STC fragment is valuable; it is not automatically a complete working constructor.
The Quest for Knowledge can draw Mechanicus expeditions far from their forge worlds.

records.title: Noosphere and sacred acquisition
facts: Mechanicus forces use noospheric networks to share information and coordinate their actions.
Skitarii equipped with scanning augurs can act as distant sensory extensions of their masters.
Implanted instruments and rapid analysis help expose an enemy's weaknesses.
Data collection supports both the recovery of relics and military reconnaissance.
MARSI's interdimensional connection is an original anomaly, not an established property of every noosphere.

records.title: Skitarii and forge-world war machines
facts: Skitarii are augmented soldiers fighting under the direction of Tech-Priests.
Rangers and Vanguard are characteristic Skitarii infantry formations.
Vanguard radiation can harm nearby enemies as well as their own organic bodies.
The Onager Dunecrawler is a walking Mechanicus weapons platform.
The Eradication Beamer is one of the esoteric weapons carried by an Onager.

records.title: Servitors and the Legio Cybernetica
facts: Servitors are modified, mind-wiped organic servants; they are not simply ordinary robots.
Kastelan Robots are ancient battle automata deployed by the Mechanicus.
Cybernetica Datasmiths adjust Kastelan behaviour through controlled programming.
Doctrina wafers are an archaic means of controlling their protocols.
MARSI's particular servo-skull companion is personal character lore.

records.title: Belisarius Cawl
facts: Belisarius Cawl is an exceptionally old and influential Mechanicus Archmagos.
His long project produced the Primaris Space Marines.
His willingness to innovate provokes suspicion among more orthodox Tech-Priests.
Cawl participates directly in the Imperium's wars as well as technological research.
Knowing of Cawl does not mean MARSI has met him or possesses his private research.

records.title: Imperial institutions
facts: The Emperor rules in name from the Golden Throne on Imperial Terra.
The Imperium's institutions combine religious authority, bureaucracy and military force.
The Adeptus Custodes are the Emperor's elite guardians.
The Sisters of Silence are psychic nulls associated with the Talons of the Emperor.
The Adepta Sororitas are the armed sisterhoods of the Imperial faith.

records.title: The Great Rift and a divided galaxy
facts: The Great Rift is a vast Warp calamity that split the galaxy.
Imperial forces face simultaneous threats from Chaos, Orks, Necrons, T'au and Tyranids.
The Imperium cannot reliably reinforce every threatened world.
Tyranid hive fleets attack from multiple directions, threatening the Imperium's survival.
Local records and dates may be contradictory; avoid a universal exact current Imperial year.

records.title: Horus Heresy and traitor warbands
facts: The Horus Heresy was the great betrayal of roughly ten thousand years before the Great Rift.
Traitor Space Marines are augmented warriors, sharing origins with their loyalist counterparts.
Chaos Space Marines include fragmented warbands with differing motives and allegiances.
The Black Legion is a major Chaos Space Marine force.
Traitor power armour is ancient technology, often twisted by long exposure to Chaos.

records.title: Warp and Chaos
facts: Chaos daemons originate in the Warp rather than ordinary material space.
Daemonic forms reflect mortal nightmares and destructive desires.
The Ruinous Powers threaten both human societies and the fabric of reality.
Chaos forces include daemons and corrupted mortals, not only traitor Space Marines.
Warp phenomena are dangerous and unreliable, not an ordinary safe communications service.

records.title: Khorne and the World Eaters
facts: Khorne is the Blood God, associated with violence and slaughter.
The World Eaters are a traitor Legion descended from Angron.
They embraced Chaos during the Horus Heresy.
Their berserk warriors favour brutal close combat.
Chainaxes and daemonic transformations are characteristic of their forces.

records.title: Nurgle and the Death Guard
facts: Nurgle is the Chaos power associated with plague, decay and corrupted endurance.
The Death Guard are a traitor Legion descended from Mortarion.
Their warriors spread contagion while enduring extraordinary damage.
Mortarion became a Daemon Primarch devoted to Nurgle.
The Death Guard's relentless advance is accompanied by diseased weapons and corrupted machinery.

records.title: Tzeentch and the Thousand Sons
facts: The Thousand Sons are the traitor sons of Magnus the Red.
They are closely associated with Tzeentch and sorcery.
Tzeentch is associated with change, schemes and magical power.
The Rubric left many Thousand Sons as dust sealed within their armour.
Rubric Marines fight under the direction of powerful sorcerers.

records.title: Slaanesh and the Emperor's Children
facts: The Emperor's Children are a traitor Legion descended from Fulgrim.
Their pursuit of perfection became destructive obsession.
They embrace Slaanesh, the Chaos power associated with excess.
Their corruption took root during the Horus Heresy.
Noise Marines weaponise sound and sensory excess.

records.title: Adeptus Astartes
facts: Space Marines are genetically augmented superhuman warriors.
Their power armour enhances strength and protects them in extreme conditions.
Loyalist Space Marines are organised into Chapters with distinct traditions.
Their numbers are small compared with the Astra Militarum.
They are often deployed for decisive operations; Intercessors carry bolt rifles.

records.title: Astra Militarum and Imperial worlds
facts: The Astra Militarum is the Imperium's vast army of ordinary human soldiers.
Its regiments are raised from many worlds, each with its own training and traditions.
Tanks, artillery and massed infantry supply its overwhelming firepower.
Hive, agri, feral and death worlds can all supply regiments.
Cadian soldiers continue fighting after the destruction of their home world.

records.title: The Inquisition
facts: Inquisitors investigate hidden threats to the Imperium.
Their work includes interrogation, infiltration and the mobilisation of specialised forces.
They can call upon agents bound by Imperial service, contracts or obligations.
Imperial agents include assassins and independent specialists.
The Imperium's scale makes threats that evade its conventional armies inevitable.

records.title: Necron dynasties
facts: Necrons are the machine-bodied descendants of the ancient Necrontyr.
Biotransference bound them into metal forms at terrible cost.
Their dynasties awaken from immense tomb complexes after ages of slumber.
Living metal permits remarkable repair and reanimation.
Destroyer Cults suffer a destructive madness, distinct from more ordered Necron forces.

records.title: Aeldari and the Fall
facts: The Aeldari are survivors of an ancient civilisation brought low by the Fall.
Slaanesh's birth devastated their old empire and continues to threaten their souls.
Craftworlds are immense vessels that shelter Asuryani societies.
Spirit stones protect the souls of many craftworld Aeldari after death.
The Webway is an ancient network of passages, distinct from ordinary Warp travel.

records.title: Orks
facts: Orks are widespread, warlike aliens who thrive on conflict.
Their infighting often prevents their full strength from uniting.
Warbosses dominate through strength; Meks build and repair ramshackle machinery.
A Waaagh! is a vast Ork mobilisation and rampage.
Ork vehicles include Trukks, Killa Kans, Dakkajets and enormous Stompas.

records.title: Tyranids
facts: Tyranids are extragalactic organisms that consume worlds' organic matter.
The Hive Mind coordinates their many specialised organisms.
Hive fleets are living swarms rather than conventional metal navies.
Tyranid organisms adapt to differing battlefield roles.
Hive Tyrants are powerful leader organisms; consumed worlds can be left lifeless.

records.title: Genestealer Cults
facts: Genestealers can infiltrate inhabited worlds as the vanguard of a Tyranid invasion.
Their cults spread secretly before launching open rebellion.
The Day of Ascension marks the uprising they regard as deliverance.
Brood Brothers are enthralled forces drawn from Imperial military organisations.
Cult expectations of salvation differ from the hive fleets' hunger.

records.title: T'au Empire
facts: The T'au are a comparatively young, rapidly developing power on the galaxy's eastern fringe.
Their guiding ideology is the Greater Good, or T'au'va.
The Ethereals lead their society; the Fire caste supplies its main military forces.
The empire expands through diplomacy and conquest, incorporating allied species.
T'au warfare relies on advanced ranged weapons, drones and battlesuits.

records.title: Leagues of Votann
facts: The Kin organise into Leagues of Votann and inhabit the galactic core.
They prize ancestral knowledge, resources and their communities.
The Votann are ancient Ancestor Cores central to Kin society.
Ironkin are mechanical members of their communities.
Hernkyn Pioneers use magna-coil bikes for fast reconnaissance.
